problem: Existing household benchmarks require per-object goal annotations, ignore user placement preferences, lack mobility (navigation plus manipulation), and lack photorealistic, physically realistic scenes, so integrated language-to-action tidying cannot be evaluated end to end.
motivation: Household tidying needs preference-aware object sorting, cross-room navigation and manipulation together. Real-world data collection is costly, so sim-to-real training needs scenes that are both photorealistic and physically consistent. 3D Gaussian Splatting offers photorealism and cross-view consistency, and pairing it with collision meshes gives physics.
key_idea: Build a benchmark of 500 3DGS-mesh hybrid household scenes in Isaac Sim, where tidying is formulated as a VLM-generated 'Action (Object, Container)' list that drives VLA manipulation and VLN navigation, with demonstration data for training and evaluation.
insight: Pretrained VLAs (RDT, pi0.5) generalize far better than non-pretrained ACT to unseen scenes and objects. Adding 100 synthetic RoboTidy demos to 50 real demos raises real-world tidying SR from 5/12 to 8/12, and 100 synthetic demos alone reach 4/12, so the sim data transfers. Making object sorting explicit in the instruction improves simulation SR/VSSR under both ZS and FS (e.g. FS SR 70.1 to 81.3), since it narrows container-selection errors. Note that some numbers are odd: the paper's VLN text and tables disagree on the NaVid-base R2R SR (0.22 vs 0.11 on RoboTidy) and the claimed drop from 0.22 to 0.16 mixes base and finetuned models.
method: 3DGS-mesh hybrid scenes: 500 InteriorGS scenes (living room, bedroom, kitchen) rendered as 3DGS (USDZ via 3DGUT), with artist meshes convex-decomposed by CoACD into invisible collision bodies in Isaac Sim 5.0

Object sorting: Qwen2.5-VL-72B parses multi-view observations into code-style prompts, induces placement rules from observed object-container pairs, and outputs an Action (Object, Container) list for new items, in zero-shot or few-shot mode

Manipulation module: four primitives (Pick and Place, Pick and Toss, Open, Close) generated by IK plus a collision-free motion planner; logs multi-view RGB, joints and gripper as VLA demos (6.4k in simulation, 400 real)

Navigation module: A* on the 2D semantic map plus PID tracking generates 1.5k trajectories, one per room pair per scene; VLMs predict velocity commands from RGB and instructions, with a PPO policy for low-level joint control
Language instructions: template-based manipulation commands; navigation instructions are hierarchical (LLM-generated high-level landmark instruction plus low-level action steps)
Metrics: OPA (container-choice accuracy) and VSSR (valid container AND completed actions) for sorting; SR/OSR/SPL for navigation; success rate for manipulation
Sim2real testbed: Cobot-Magic dual-arm platform with RDT, comparing 50 real, 50 real + 100 sim, and 100 sim demos

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-72B (frozen, sorting); RDT/pi0.5/ACT (fine-tuned, manipulation); NaVid-7B and NaVILA-8B (fine-tuned, navigation)
setting.training_data: Sorting: none (ZS) or 2 examples per container (FS). Manipulation: 100 demos per action from RoboTidy simulation. Navigation: fine-tuned on 300 scenes (0.9k trajectory-instruction pairs).
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (640x480) for navigation; multi-view RGB plus joint states for manipulation; optional depth/LiDAR
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands (navigation); joint-level trajectories for the aloha-agilex bimanual robot (manipulation)
setting.privileged: none at test time for navigation (no map supplied); the sorting evaluation uses a scene's closed candidate container set

numbers.eval_set_note: the ~200 held-out RoboTidy scenes not used for fine-tuning (300 used for training)

numbers_note: The real-world E1 results appear only in a figure. Navigation numbers are printed as fractions (0.26 etc.). OSR/SPL in Table 2 are inconsistent in places (e.g. OSR lower than SR for NaVILA-R).
results: On the RoboTidy benchmark, the best VLN model (NaVILA-R) reaches only 0.26 SR, and NaVILA-base gets 0.22 against 0.29 on R2R-CE val-unseen, so the benchmark is harder. Fine-tuning on RoboTidy yields 0.31 SR on R2R-CE val-unseen against 0.29 for NaVILA-base. pi0.5 reaches 85-98% success across the four manipulation primitives, well above ACT at 6-24%. Sorting with Qwen2.5-VL-72B reaches 92.7 OPA (ZS) and 94.6 (FS), compared with TidyBot's 90.7 (ZS) and 85.7 (FS).
limitations: Sim-to-real gap remains, and the real-world evaluation is small (12 objects, 10 trials per action) and did not cover complex lighting and backgrounds
Only four manipulation primitives, static scenes, and three room types; no dynamic obstacles or human interference
Reported results and text are inconsistent in places, and the navigation evaluation has low absolute SR with limited baselines
